h1: Rodent Exclusion in San Leandro, CA
description: Rodent exclusion in San Leandro, CA: structural sealing of every penetration, then cleanup and reinsulation. Get a free inspection and estimate.
intro: Rodent exclusion for East Bay homes after an infestation: we structurally seal every penetration, remove the contaminated insulation, sanitize the space, and only then reinsulate. Seal first, clean, reinsulate, in that order.
hero_alt: Sealed attic penetration after rodent exclusion

paragraphs: Exclusion is what you need when rodents have already been inside: every penetration gets sealed, the contaminated material comes out, the space is sanitized, and only then does new insulation go in.
The order matters. Sealing first stops the source, cleaning removes what they left, and reinsulation finishes the job on a secure, sanitary attic.

sections.h2: Sealing every penetration, not just the obvious ones
paragraphs: Rodents use openings most people never see: the gap behind a gutter, the chase around a vent pipe, the crack at a roof-to-wall junction. We seal all of them, not just the one they came through last time.
bullets: Garage, crawl space and foundation openings
Hardware cloth and metal flashing where rodents chew

paragraphs: Rodent droppings, urine-soaked insulation and nesting material have to go. We vacuum out the contaminated insulation, remove the debris, and sanitize the deck and framing.
Contaminated waste is bagged and disposed of properly, and the cleanup is part of the same fixed estimate as the sealing.

sections.h2: Reinsulating after the space is secure
paragraphs: New insulation only goes in after the sealing is done and the attic is clean and dry. Insulating first would hand the next rodent fresh bedding.
We reinsulate to the R-value your house needs, with depth markers, so the finished attic is documented and verifiable.
After the work, we re-check every sealed point and walk the house for anything we missed. Photos of the sealed openings go to you with notes on the seasonal spots to watch.
If activity ever reappears, the sealed map from your job tells us exactly where to look first.

steps.name: Inspect
steps.text: We map every penetration and the extent of the rodent damage, then quote the full exclusion and cleanup as one fixed estimate.
steps.image_alt: Mapping rodent entry points and damage

steps.name: Seal
steps.text: Every penetration is closed with flashing, hardware cloth and sealant, starting with the largest openings.
steps.image_alt: Sealing a penetration with hardware cloth

steps.name: Clean
steps.text: Contaminated insulation and droppings are vacuumed out, and the deck and framing are sanitized.

steps.name: Reinsulate
steps.text: Fresh insulation goes in to the target R-value, and we document the sealed points and the finished attic.

faqs.q: What is the difference between rodent proofing and exclusion?
faqs.a: Proofing seals the building so rodents never get in. Exclusion is the full job after an infestation: seal every penetration, remove contaminated material, sanitize, then reinsulate.

faqs.q: Do you remove the contaminated insulation?
faqs.a: Yes. Rodent-soiled insulation is vacuumed out and properly disposed of as part of the exclusion job, and it is included in the fixed estimate.

faqs.q: In what order does the work happen?
faqs.a: Seal first, then clean and sanitize, then reinsulate. That sequence is what keeps the attic rodent-free after the job.

faqs.q: Will new insulation attract rodents again?
faqs.a: Not once the building is sealed. Rodents return through openings, and exclusion closes them. That is why sealing happens before any new material goes in.
Most exclusion jobs finish in one to two days depending on the size of the attic and the extent of the damage. The estimate states the schedule.

faqs.q: Do you set traps or use bait?
faqs.a: No. We exclude rodents by sealing the building so they cannot enter or return, then restore the attic. That approach removes the access instead of chasing individual animals.
